children: Apollo and Goldman Sachs have priced a roughly $44 billion debt package to finance SpaceX's acquisition of Nvidia's GPU chips and related equipment, marking what the firms said is the largest AI-related chip financing ever arranged.

Investor demand exceeded supply, allowing the transaction to be upsized. The proceeds are expected to help bankroll SpaceX's deployment of Nvidia's next-generation Vera Rubin chips as it expands its terrestrial AI computing footprint.
The $25.17 billion of senior secured A3 notes maturing in April 2033 priced at a yield of 8.259%, according to a source familiar with the sale.
About $4.4 billion of senior secured A2 notes maturing in April 2031 were sold at 7.66%, the source said, while $2.564 billion of class B subordinated secured April 2033 notes were sold at 8.36%.
The deal underscores the large capital requirements of the AI boom as technology companies race to secure advanced processors and build out computing infrastructure needed to support AI development.
Lease schedules are expected to start when the GPUs and related equipment are delivered in the first half of 2027
BlackRock, Goldman Sachs Asset Management and accounts advised by KKR provided anchor commitments for the transaction, the statement said.
SpaceX said last month that an affiliate of Apollo Global Management would buy AI chips and server hardware and lease them to the company in a deal with total principal payments of about $40 billion.
